meta.scale: 0 = durable / human-anchored, 1 = highly automatable by current (2026) AI
meta.framing: Editorial estimates of how exposed each O*NET work activity is to today's AI (LLMs + mature automation), NOT a prediction of job loss. Cognitive/routine information work scores high; interpersonal care, physical dexterity in unstructured settings, and accountable judgment score low. Robotics is treated as slower/costlier than software AI, so physical activities stay comparatively durable.
sources: Frey & Osborne (2017), The Future of Employment
Eloundou et al. (2023), GPTs are GPTs: labor-market exposure of LLMs
Brynjolfsson, Mitchell & Rock — Suitability for Machine Learning (SML) rubric
OECD (2023) and recent GenAI task-exposure analyses
meta.review: Authored by FlightWay (Igor + CTO). Reviewable and versioned; adjust weights here, then rerun `npm run onet:exposure`.

4.A.1.a.1.name: Getting Information
4.A.1.a.1.why: Information retrieval and synthesis is a core LLM strength.

4.A.1.a.2.name: Monitoring Processes, Materials, or Surroundings
4.A.1.a.2.why: Sensors and vision automate parts; physical presence and judgment often remain.

4.A.1.b.1.name: Identifying Objects, Actions, and Events
4.A.1.b.1.why: Computer vision handles many recognition tasks.

4.A.1.b.2.name: Inspecting Equipment, Structures, or Materials
4.A.1.b.2.why: Vision assists, but hands-on inspection and edge cases stay human.

4.A.1.b.3.name: Estimating the Quantifiable Characteristics of Products, Events, or Information

4.A.2.a.1.name: Judging the Qualities of Objects, Services, or People
4.A.2.a.1.why: Subjective, context-laden judgment resists full automation.

4.A.2.a.2.name: Processing Information
4.A.2.a.2.why: Canonical routine cognitive work — highly automatable.

4.A.2.a.3.name: Evaluating Information to Determine Compliance with Standards
4.A.2.a.3.why: Rule-checking against standards is largely codifiable.

4.A.2.a.4.name: Analyzing Data or Information
4.A.2.a.4.why: AI is strong at analysis; humans still frame and verify.

4.A.2.b.1.name: Making Decisions and Solving Problems
4.A.2.b.1.why: AI assists, but accountability and novel judgment stay human.

4.A.2.b.2.name: Thinking Creatively
4.A.2.b.2.why: GenAI drafts, but originality, taste, and direction remain human-led.

4.A.2.b.3.name: Updating and Using Relevant Knowledge
4.A.2.b.3.why: Knowledge lookup automates; applied expertise less so.

4.A.2.b.4.name: Developing Objectives and Strategies
4.A.2.b.4.why: Strategy needs context, stakes, and ownership AI lacks.

4.A.2.b.6.name: Organizing, Planning, and Prioritizing Work
4.A.2.b.6.why: Planning tools help; prioritization under ambiguity stays human.

4.A.3.a.1.name: Performing General Physical Activities
4.A.3.a.1.why: Physical work; robotics is slow and costly to deploy.

4.A.3.a.2.name: Handling and Moving Objects
4.A.3.a.2.why: Dexterous manipulation in unstructured settings is hard for robots.

4.A.3.a.3.name: Controlling Machines and Processes
4.A.3.a.3.why: Process automation is mature in structured environments.

4.A.3.a.4.name: Operating Vehicles, Mechanized Devices, or Equipment
4.A.3.a.4.why: Autonomy is improving but deployment is gradual.

4.A.3.b.1.name: Working with Computers
4.A.3.b.1.why: Digital tasks are highly automatable (and AI's native surface).

4.A.3.b.2.name: Drafting, Laying Out, and Specifying Technical Devices, Parts, and Equipment

4.A.3.b.4.name: Repairing and Maintaining Mechanical Equipment
4.A.3.b.4.why: Hands-on repair in varied conditions stays human.

4.A.3.b.5.name: Repairing and Maintaining Electronic Equipment
4.A.3.b.5.why: Diagnosis aided by AI; physical repair remains manual.

4.A.3.b.6.name: Documenting/Recording Information
4.A.3.b.6.why: Drafting and record-keeping are core LLM strengths.

4.A.4.a.1.name: Interpreting the Meaning of Information for Others
4.A.4.a.1.why: Summarization automates; trusted interpretation stays human.

4.A.4.a.2.name: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates
4.A.4.a.2.why: Workplace communication is relational and contextual.

4.A.4.a.3.name: Communicating with People Outside the Organization
4.A.4.a.3.why: External comms drafts automate; relationships do not.

4.A.4.a.4.name: Establishing and Maintaining Interpersonal Relationships
4.A.4.a.4.why: Trust and relationships are durable human work.

4.A.4.a.5.name: Assisting and Caring for Others
4.A.4.a.5.why: Care work depends on human presence and empathy.

4.A.4.a.6.name: Selling or Influencing Others
4.A.4.a.6.why: AI supports outreach; persuasion and rapport stay human.

4.A.4.a.7.name: Resolving Conflicts and Negotiating with Others
4.A.4.a.7.why: High-stakes negotiation needs human trust and judgment.

4.A.4.a.8.name: Performing for or Working Directly with the Public

4.A.4.b.1.name: Coordinating the Work and Activities of Others
4.A.4.b.1.why: Coordination tooling helps; accountability stays human.

4.A.4.b.3.name: Training and Teaching Others
4.A.4.b.3.why: AI tutors assist; mentorship and modeling stay human.

4.A.4.b.4.name: Guiding, Directing, and Motivating Subordinates
4.A.4.b.4.why: Leadership and motivation are durable human roles.

4.A.4.b.5.name: Coaching and Developing Others
4.A.4.b.5.why: Developmental coaching depends on human relationship.

4.A.4.b.6.name: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others
4.A.4.b.6.why: AI drafts advice; accountable counsel stays human.

4.A.4.c.2.name: Staffing Organizational Units
4.A.4.c.2.why: Screening automates; hiring judgment and accountability remain.

4.A.4.c.3.name: Monitoring and Controlling Resources
4.A.4.c.3.why: Tracking automates; allocation decisions stay human.
